identity: The adopted 2026–2027 VU regulations govern the ordinary Dutch-taught Biomedical Sciences bachelor (Biomedische Wetenschappen), with no formal graduation specialisation. NVAO decision AV-3411 approved the name change associated with the Dutch language transition, retaining the previous accreditation decision. The regulations identify current RIO 56990. The frozen registry retains historical identifier 59324. The programme lineage is established without assuming equality of those identifiers. The curriculum comprises 18 prescribed 6 EC courses, three separate 6 EC restricted choices, 30 EC open minor space and one 24 EC thesis. The displayed choices follow the first-listed eligible options. Lab safety and Dutch language assessment are mandatory without additional credit and gate the Microbiology grade. Research in Biomedical Sciences gates Statistics and Methodology. Microbiology and Immunology gate the optional Infectious Diseases course. Thesis entry requires all 60 EC from year one, at least 42 EC from year two, an approved project and supervisor, registration and completed OnStage approval. The ordinary first-year study advice threshold is 42 EC with applicable exceptions. Individual courses may be taught in English. The Immunology course also requires prior lab safety for registration. Individual open choices require prior Board approval, at least 12 EC at level 300 and at most 6 EC at level 100. Listed university minors may be taken without prior Board approval subject to entry requirements. Foreign choices have the same level rules and may include one 6 EC master-level course subject to the regulations.
ledger: First-listed of three restricted 6-EC year-one choices (Biomedische Wetenschappen en de Maatschappij, Science Communication, Biochemisch onderzoek); selected for this valid pathway.
First-listed of four restricted 6-EC year-two choices (Pathophysiology of heart and circulation, Big data, International Public Health, Science Communication).
Genuinely open academic 30-EC third-year minor/profiling space; no optional minor is imposed.
First-listed of four restricted 6-EC year-three choices in the adopted OER (Epidemiology, Human Neurophysiology, Management of Innovations, Infectious Diseases).

Selected 24 EC Experimental thesis: independently conduct supervised laboratory, observational or computer-modelling research in an approved scientific programme; lab journal, scientific report, oral and poster presentations. All 60 EC from year one plus at least 42 EC from year two; enrolment and completed OnStage approval before start. Go/no-go at 4–6 weeks. Professional development sufficient and research 40%, report 35%, oral 20%, poster 5%; each partial grade at least 5.5. February starters have a compulsory poster symposium. Data Analysis is a mutually exclusive alternative, not an additional 24 EC requirement.
accounting: Year one and year two each contain nine required 6 EC courses and one restricted 6 EC choice. Year three has 30 EC open choice, one restricted 6 EC choice and one 24 EC thesis. There are 23 unique components totalling 180 EC. The zero-credit laboratory safety and language requirements are separately recorded. The programme has no graduation tracks.
progression: OER articles 9.1, 11.3–11.4, 12 and 14.1 control. First-listed choices are Biomedische Wetenschappen en de Maatschappij, cardiovascular pathophysiology, Epidemiology and Experimental thesis. Cardiovascular and respiratory anatomy and physiology are recommended preparation for the heart course. Earlier anatomy and physiology provides this background. The thesis requires full year one and at least 42 EC of year two, approved supervision and project, and registration and complete OnStage processing. It includes a 4–6 week go/no-go and a four-part assessment with each component at least 5.5 and sufficient professionalism. February entrants attend the poster symposium.
interestAccounting: All 57 target rows reviewed. Eleven can generate responses, of which eight are core-owned and three receive explicit candidate outcomes. Twenty-eight are supporting topics and eighteen are search-only illustrations or outcomes. Current sources confirm that candidate labels and career wording do not imply formal tracks, licensure or admission.
